chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

Abū al-Qāsim Mukhalled ibn Mūsā al-Rāzī wrote to the man, asking him about the detached ʿumrah: is ṭawāf al-nisāʾ required upon the one performing it, and also regarding the ʿumrah by which one performs tamattuʿ up to the hajj?

So he wrote: As for the detached ʿumrah, ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is required upon the one performing it. But as for the one by which tamattuʿ is performed up to the hajj, ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is not required upon the one performing it.

key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage, in relation to which the ʿumrah of tamattuʿ is joined
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةُ الْمَبْتُولَةُ: the detached or separate ʿumrah, treated here as requiring ṭawāf al-nisāʾ
key_terms.صَاحِبِهَا: the person performing or undertaking that specific ʿumrah
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: the circumambulation connected to the lawfulness of marital relations after pilgrimage rites
key_terms.يُتَمَتَّعُ بِهَا: the ʿumrah performed as part of tamattuʿ leading into hajj

ai.seo_question: Is ṭawāf al-nisāʾ obligatory in every type of ʿumrah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ṭawāf al-nisāʾ in different types of ʿumrah. It states that ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is obligatory in al-ʿumrah al-mabtūlah, but it is not obligatory in the ʿumrah of tamattuʿ connected to hajj. The narration is significant in distinguishing the rulings of separate forms of pilgrimage worship.
